findings.title: The headline asks for trust, but the page does not back it with who works out the tides or where the data comes from

location.description: the headline and the "Lock gate times" note

findings.viewer_experience: A harbor master reads "can stand behind", then "Gate openings are worked out" with no one doing the working out. They cannot tell whether this means more work for the office or a black box they cannot vouch for.

current.value: "Gate openings are worked out from each tide" has no subject, and no line says where the tide data comes from or what the office checks

findings.target: The verb in the Lock gate times note has a subject, and one line says where the tide data comes from and what the office checks or approves. The maker must supply the source of the tide data and what the office checks; they are not on the page.
findings.fix_direction: Give "worked out" its subject in the Lock gate times note. Add one line that says where the tide data comes from and what the office checks or approves. Only the maker has these facts.
findings.source: Nielsen: match between the system and the real world; plain-language guidance against an agentless passive

closed_when.check: In the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports, the Lock gate times note names who or what works out the gate openings, and one line near the headline or the note says where the tide data comes from and what the office checks.

findings.title: The tide card does not say it is a sample of what berth holders see

location.description: the "Today at Porthmellin" heading above the tide table

findings.viewer_experience: A visitor can read the card as today's real tides or as a weather widget, not as the page their berth holders will see.

current.value: No line under the "Today at Porthmellin" heading at any viewport

findings.target: One short line under the heading says the table is a sample of what berth holders see.
findings.fix_direction: Add one short line under "Today at Porthmellin" that says this is a sample of what berth holders see.

closed_when.check: In the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports, a short line under "Today at Porthmellin" says the table is a sample of what berth holders see.

findings.title: The tide card is cramped at 298 px wide

location.description: the tide card on the right of the hero

findings.viewer_experience: The Time and Height columns are 67 px and 63 px wide, so the numbers sit close together, and the page's best evidence looks like a small sidebar.
findings.target: The card spans the second and third feature columns and stays on the grid (left edge at x 491 on desktop, x 811 on widescreen).
findings.fix_direction: Make the card span the second and third feature columns, from x 491 on desktop and x 811 on widescreen, so it stays on the grid and gets its width back.

closed_when.check: In the desktop and widescreen viewports, the tide card's left edge is at x 491 (desktop) and x 811 (widescreen), matching the second feature column, and the Time and Height columns are wider than 67 px and 63 px.

findings.title: On the tablet the content stops at x 624 while the nav ends at x 704

location.description: the tablet hero, card and notes column, whose right edge falls 80 px short of the nav

findings.viewer_experience: The right edge of the content no longer lines up with the nav, and an 80 px empty strip sits down the right side.

current.value: content right edge at x 624; nav right edge at x 704

findings.target: The content column runs the full 640 px between the nav's edges, to x 704.
findings.fix_direction: Let the content column run the full 640 px between the nav's edges. The notes still read well at that width.

closed_when.check: In the tablet viewport, the right edge of h1 and the hero text box is at x 704, matching the right edge of nav.site-nav > a:nth-of-type(4).
